package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that disables Windows Defender and other security protections, downloads and executes a known trojan/cryptominer, and attempts anti-forensics. The package is published by an untrustworthy account and masquerades as a legitimate utility.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when checker.js is loaded as part of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Heavily obfuscated JavaScript code using JSDefender, which upon deobfuscation executes multiple Windows batch commands to disable security features.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Runs a series of batch commands to disable Windows Defender, tamper protection, real-time protection, and other security services by modifying registry keys and stopping services.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security protections is a classic precursor to further malicious activity, such as malware installation or data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should not attempt to alter system security settings or modify the Windows registry.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployment scripts may disable security for compatibility, but never in a userland npm package.
key_indicators: Batch commands to stop/disable security services

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a trojanized Discord.exe binary from a Discord CDN link and places it in the Windows startup folder for persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and persisting an unknown executable from a remote source is a hallmark of malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should never download or install binaries outside their own directory, especially not to system startup locations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in the context of a public npm package.
key_indicators: Use of Discord CDN for malware hosting

execution_context.trigger: import-time (as part of checker.js execution, after Discord.exe drop)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a remove.cmd script from Discord CDN, which repeats the Defender-disabling commands for redundancy.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redundant disabling of security features is a strong indicator of persistence and anti-detection intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should download and execute remote scripts that alter system security.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when Discord.exe is executed at system startup)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: public static void Main() { ... encrypted payload ... }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes encrypted .NET code, likely a cryptominer or trojan, with the decryption key packed inside for runtime decryption and execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypted payloads in binaries are a common malware evasion technique. The use of Discord.exe as a filename is also suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not self-decrypt and execute hidden payloads, especially from a dropped binary.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or commercial software may use encryption, but not in this context.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the flame-vali npm package, triggering execution of checker.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: System security protections are disabled, opening the system to further compromise.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and persists a trojanized Discord.exe binary to the Windows startup folder.
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojan will execute on next system startup, establishing persistence.

attack_chain.action: A remove.cmd script is downloaded and executed, redundantly disabling security features.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ensures security protections remain disabled, even if initial commands failed.

attack_chain.action: Discord.exe runs at startup, decrypts and executes its malicious payload (likely cryptominer/trojan).
attack_chain.leads_to: System is compromised, attacker achieves final goal (e.g., cryptomining, remote access, data theft).

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm packages that spawns shell commands
Batch commands targeting Windows Defender and registry keys
Network requests to Discord CDN for executable/script downloads
Dropping executables to Windows startup folders
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for obfuscated JavaScript that spawns shell commands, especially those modifying Windows Defender settings or downloading executables/scripts from Discord CDN. Flag any package that writes to Windows startup folders or drops binaries named Discord.exe. Alert on registry modifications under Windows Defender keys and on network requests to Discord CDN for suspicious file types.
